EARLY-WARNING RESEARCH / FICTIONAL INDIA REGIONS

Seven-day incident forecasting baseline

Learn from earlier records. Forecast later outcomes. Count the errors.

SYNTHETIC DATA ONLY

This working statistical model learns from authored regional records. It does not predict real attacks. The data, labels and relationships are fictional; real historical validation is still required.

Chronological experiment

240 weekly fictional records. Train on the first 160; exclude the next record as a time gap; issue forecasts for 79 later records. Training outcomes must be known before the first test forecast. Feature scaling is learned from training records only.

The logistic baseline estimates an authored incident outcome within seven days using warning-group counts, repost counts, contradicting-group counts and source coverage. These features are experimental assumptions, not established predictors of terrorism.

Fixed review threshold: 0.35. Coverage below 0.40 causes abstention. These are toy experiment settings and do not authorize an operational alert.

Inspect a fictional input

Fixed fictional region IN-1. No person, real site, weapons, threat attribution or live-source data enters this model. Changing these authored inputs does not change an analyst workspace.

What operational early warning still requires

A defined incident target and geographic/time horizon; permitted historical source snapshots; independently checked later outcomes; time-based external testing; reliability and false-alarm analysis; drift monitoring; and a reviewed human response process. Prevention effectiveness is a separate outcome to evaluate.

Probability error combines several properties. A lower Brier score alone does not establish calibration. See the reliability bins and the baseline comparison together.
